title: Paired Pixels, Balanced Rows, Trimmed Boxes, Lagging Slices & One Toast
description: A sprite morph written as keyframes, rows that refuse an orphan, type trimmed to its caps, slices that lag, and one toast that morphs.

drops.title: Every Pixel Is Paired
drops.description: Two pixel sprites, one box-shadow: pixels are matched, interpolated and written out as a generated @keyframes rule.
drops.concept: morphin pairs each lit pixel of one sprite with a pixel of the other — by nearest neighbour, by diagonal, by brightness — then tweens the pair and emits the whole flight as CSS. This reimplementation generates the rule live: pick a matching strategy, a frame count and a hold, and watch the keyframe text (and its size) change. Playback is pure CSS, stepped so it keeps the pixel-art snap.
drops.source: javierbyte/morphin — pixel art interpolations embedded with only CSS

interaction.mouse: Change the matching strategy, frames, cycle, pixel size and hold; every edit regenerates the CSS
interaction.click: Pick a pixel-matching method from the select to re-pair the sprites
interaction.touch: All controls are sliders and selects — the panel stacks under the sprites on small screens

drops.title: No Orphan Rows
drops.description: flex-wrap: balance keeps the line count and spreads items evenly, and flex-line-count sets a floor on the number of lines.
drops.concept: Greedy wrapping fills each line to the brim and strands the remainder alone. Chrome 150's flex-wrap: balance keeps the same number of lines and redistributes across them. Three rows — icons, tags and a nav — flip between the two modes at any width, and where the value is missing the same rule runs in JS: find the natural line count, binary-search the smallest max line width that still fits it, insert real breaks. Both paths produce identical rows.
drops.source: Ahmad Shadeed — “Balancing flex items with flex-wrap: balance”

interaction.mouse: Toggle wrap vs balance, drag the container width, raise the minimum line count
interaction.click: The segmented control switches the wrapping mode on all three rows at once
interaction.touch: Rows reflow to the phone width; the readout under each says how many lines resulted

drops.title: The Reset That Trims the Box
drops.description: text-box cuts the half-leading, text-wrap balances and de-orphans, and the hyphenation limits make hyphens: auto usable.
drops.concept: A modern typography reset, made visible. Each specimen is painted with a tinted background, so switching on text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic visibly shrinks the block from its line-height box down to cap-height-to-baseline — about 13px off a display heading here. text-wrap: balance, text-wrap: pretty, hanging-punctuation and the hyphenate-limit-* family each get a switch, with live support pills saying which the browser actually honours.
drops.source: CSS-Tricks — “Taming Typography: Building a Modern CSS Reset”

interaction.mouse: Flip each property on and off and watch the painted box and the line count change
interaction.click: Toggle switches apply the property to all four specimens at once
interaction.touch: Drag the measure slider to change the column width and re-break every specimen

drops.title: Parts That Lag
drops.description: An image sliced into bands that each carry the same background at a different offset and slide on hover with their own delay.
drops.concept: puffin.js never transforms the picture. It cuts it into parts, each a window onto the same image, and gives every part its own offset, duration and delay so a hover shears the picture apart and back. Here the artwork is drawn procedurally into a data URL, the slice count and shear pattern are tunable, and the motion is nothing but CSS transitions with staggered transition-delay.
drops.source: Treast/puffin.js — a new way to hover images

interaction.mouse: Hover any of the three cards to shear it; tune slices, offset, stagger, duration, pattern and easing
interaction.click: Press and hold works the same as hover for the shear
interaction.touch: Tap and hold a card to hold the shear open; the panel stacks below on small screens

drops.title: One Toast, Morphing
drops.description: The next call changes the toast already on screen — icon, text, height and progress spring to the new shape instead of stacking.
drops.concept: ding keeps a single toast and patches it, with size, shape and position on a spring solver so an interrupted animation keeps its momentum. This rebuild runs one semi-implicit Euler spring per animated value — height, lift, opacity — measures the new content and springs the box to it, and draws a live trace of the height spring. Three preset pucks let you feel stiffness and damping on their own.
drops.source: YusufCeng1z/ding — toasts with real spring physics

interaction.mouse: Fire success, error, loading, a promise, a progress run or an action toast — all into the same box
interaction.click: Click the pucks to launch three different spring tunings side by side
interaction.touch: Buttons wrap to the phone width and the toast sits above the credit bar
